statement: The command tally shall report how long each text file that the user names is, measured as its number of lines, words and characters.
criterion: Given a text file of 3 lines, 6 words and 30 characters, running tally on it prints the counts 3, 6 and 30 for that file.

statement: The command tally shall read each file that the user names and print, for each file, its number of lines, words and characters, and shall print a total of those counts.
criterion: Given two text files with known counts, tally prints one row per file with its lines, words and characters, and a final row whose counts are the sums of the two files' counts.

statement: The command shall be invoked as tally [-l] [-w] [-c] [file...] and shall accept zero or more file names.
criterion: Running tally with zero, one and three file names, with and without each of the flags -l, -w and -c, is accepted and produces counts; each named file appears in the output.

statement: The flag -l shall select the line count, -w the word count and -c the character count; the flags may be combined, and tally shall print the selected counts in the fixed order lines, words, characters, whatever the order of the flags on the command line; with no flag, tally shall print all three counts.
criterion: For a file with known counts, tally -l prints only the line count, tally -w only the word count, tally -c only the character count; tally -c -l and tally -l -c both print the line count then the character count; tally -w -l -c and tally with no flag both print the line, word and character counts in that order.

statement: When no file name is given, tally shall read and count standard input, and the row for standard input shall end after the counts, with no name; a file name of - shall name a file called -, not standard input.
criterion: Piping a text with known counts into tally with no file name prints one row holding only the line, word and character counts of that text, with no trailing name, and the exit code is 0; running tally - in a directory that holds a file named - prints the counts of that file followed by the name -, and running it where no such file exists reports an unreadable file and exits with code 1.

statement: The output shall have one row for each file counted without an error, holding the counts that the flags select followed by the file name, each field separated from the next by exactly one space; with two files or more, a last row shall hold, in the same layout, the sum of each selected count over the files counted without an error, followed by the word total; a file that cannot be read or is not valid UTF-8 shall add nothing to the total.
criterion: For one file, the output is exactly one row of the form '<counts> <name>' with single spaces; for two files, the output is two file rows followed by a row '<sums> total'; with -w, each row holds only the word count and the name; for two readable files and one missing file, the total row holds the sums of the two readable files only.

statement: When a named file cannot be read, tally shall write a message to standard error that holds the file name and the reason, and shall end with exit code 1.
criterion: Running tally on a file that does not exist, and on a file without read permission, writes to standard error a message holding that file name and the reason (such as no such file or permission denied), and the exit code is 1.

statement: A file that cannot be read shall not stop the counting of the other named files.
criterion: Running tally on a readable file, then a missing file, then a second readable file prints the rows of both readable files with correct counts, writes the error for the missing file to standard error, and exits with code 1.

statement: When a named file is a directory, tally shall treat it as a file that cannot be read: it shall write a message to standard error that holds the name and the reason, print no row for it, add nothing to the total, and end with exit code 1.
criterion: Running tally on a readable file and a directory prints the row of the readable file and no row for the directory, writes to standard error a message holding the directory's name and the reason (such as is a directory), and the exit code is 1.

statement: When a file is not valid UTF-8, tally shall print no row for it and add nothing to the total, shall write a message to standard error that holds the file name, without a byte offset, shall still count the remaining files, and shall end with exit code 1.
criterion: Running tally on a valid file, then a file that holds an invalid UTF-8 byte sequence (such as the byte 0xFF), then a second valid file prints the rows of both valid files and no row for the invalid one, writes to standard error a message holding that file name and no byte offset, and the exit code is 1.

statement: When no error occurs, tally shall end with exit code 0.
criterion: Running tally on readable, valid UTF-8 files, and on valid standard input, ends with exit code 0.

statement: When a flag is unknown or the usage is wrong, tally shall write a usage message to standard error, count nothing, and end with exit code 2.
criterion: Running tally -x on a readable file writes a usage message to standard error, prints nothing on standard output, and the exit code is 2.

statement: The product shall be written in Go, using only the Go standard library, and shall be built with the Go toolchain.
criterion: The go.mod file declares no required module, every import is a standard-library package, and go build succeeds with the Go toolchain alone.

statement: The product shall count only lines, words and characters, and shall offer no other count such as bytes, paragraphs or sentences.
criterion: The usage accepts only the flags -l, -w and -c; any other flag, such as one for bytes, paragraphs or sentences, is rejected and no such count is printed.

statement: The product shall not unpack archives or walk directories; a file shall be treated as not text exactly when it is not valid UTF-8.
criterion: No code path unpacks an archive or walks a directory; a file of bytes that is valid UTF-8 is counted whatever its content, and a file that is not valid UTF-8 is rejected as R-009 states.

statement: The product shall be a command-line program only, with no graphical interface, network service or plug-in system.
criterion: The source imports no graphical, network-server or plug-in package (such as net/http or plugin), and the program opens no window and no listening socket.

statement: The functions that count the lines, the words and the characters of a reader shall live in a package count of the same Go module, separate from the package main of the command.
criterion: The module holds a package count, distinct from the package main, that exports the functions counting lines, words and characters of an io.Reader, and the command imports it to do its counting.

statement: A line shall be a run of characters that ends with a line feed; the last line of a file shall count as a line when the file does not end with a line feed; a line feed alone ends an empty line, which counts as one line; a carriage return before a line feed shall be part of the line and count as a character, like any other code point; an empty file shall have zero lines, zero words and zero characters.
criterion:
The text 'a
b
' counts 2 lines, 'a
b' counts 2 lines, '
' counts 1 line and '

' counts 2 lines; 'a
b
' counts 2 lines and 6 characters; an empty file counts 0 lines, 0 words and 0 characters.

statement: A word shall be a run of characters that are not white space, where white space is any character with the Unicode property White_Space.
criterion: The text 'one  two\tthree' counts 3 words; text separated by U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE or U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE splits into separate words; a text of only white space counts 0 words.

statement: A character shall be one Unicode code point of a text in UTF-8, whatever the number of bytes that encode it.
criterion: The text 'aé€😀' (1, 2, 3 and 4 bytes per code point) counts 4 characters; a combining sequence such as 'e' followed by U+0301 counts 2 characters.

statement: Counting a file of 10 MiB of ASCII text with lines of about 80 characters shall take at most 2 seconds of elapsed time for the whole process, from its start to its exit, on any computer with 4 cores and a solid-state disk, with the file already in the cache of the operating system.
criterion: A test generates a file of 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes) of ASCII text with lines of about 80 characters, reads it once to warm the cache of the operating system, then runs tally on it on a computer with 4 cores and a solid-state disk, and measures an elapsed time of the whole process, from start to exit, of at most 2 seconds.

statement: Counting a file of 1 GiB shall use at most 64 MiB of peak heap during the run.
criterion: A test that counts a generated file of 1 GiB (1,073,741,824 bytes) samples the heap in use (runtime.ReadMemStats, HeapAlloc) every 10 milliseconds during the count, and the largest sampled value is at most 64 MiB (67,108,864 bytes).

statement: The tests of the package count shall cover at least 90 percent of its statements.
criterion: The output of go test -cover for the package count reports a coverage of at least 90.0 percent of statements; the coverage of the package main is not part of the target.
